verified_clean: map16 / map256 codec shapes match the real disasm exactly: enigma-decoded map16 is 8 bytes per block (0 remainder in all 6 zones) and kosinski-decoded map256 is 512 bytes per chunk (41984 bytes / 82 chunks, 0 remainder in all 6 zones) — s1-io.ts:272-291 loops `o += 8` and `o += 512` accordingly.

Chunk-cell and block-cell bit packing is lossless on 100% of real S1 data: I round-tripped every word of all six zones' map16 and map256 through `packChunkCell(unpackChunkCell(w))` and `packBlockCell(unpackBlockCell(w))` (model.ts:150-187) — 0 mismatches. In particular bit 10 of the chunk word (which the engine's `andi.w #$7FF` at FindFloor asm:115 would honor but model.ts's BLOCK_MASK 0x3ff drops) is never set in stock data, and the editor's own 1024-block ceiling (classicLevelStore.ts:1178) keeps it that way.

The two-tier collision gate itself is modelled correctly for solidity: classic-overlays.ts:66 skips `cell.solidity === 0` before the colind lookup at :67, matching FindFloor asm:117 `btst d5,d4`; the 0/1/2/3 → none/top/sides-bottom/all mapping in `solidityFill` (classic-overlays.ts:35-42) matches the engine's d5 = $D (top) / $E (LRB) bit tests.

Chunk-cell flip semantics in the collision overlay are byte-faithful to FindFloor. X-flip: classic-overlays.ts:76 `sc = cell.xf ? 15 - c : c` == asm:139 `not.w d1` + `andi.w #$F`. Y-flip: classic-overlays.ts:80 `ry = 16 - run.y - run.h` is algebraically identical to asm:158 `neg.w d0` fed through `columnSolidRun` for every case (h>0, h<0, h=16); same for the surface line at :112-113.

Layout codec is byte-identical round-trip on all 29 real level files including the three irregular ones (mz3bg/syz1/syz3 carry one trailing byte, ending.bin is truncated) — decode/encode via s1-layout.ts:26-38 reproduced every file exactly, which SonLVL's writer does not.

Layout dimension limits match the engine's RAM: `MAX_LAYOUT_W = 64` / `MAX_LAYOUT_H = 8` (model.ts:210-211) equal `layout_row_interlaced = $40` and the 8-row buffer in s1disasm/_Constants.asm:107-108 + _Variables.asm:21; the widest real file (sbz2bg, w=60) and tallest (h=8) both fit.

Chunk addressability limit is right: `MAX_ADDRESSABLE_CHUNKS = 0x7f` (model.ts:208) is justified by FindNearestTile asm:26 `bmi .specialtile`, and every real zone ships exactly 82 chunks, so no stock zone trips the cap in `classicCommitCanvas` (classicLevelStore.ts:1068) or `classicAddChunk` (:1192).

The 1-based chunk-id shift lives in exactly one place and every consumer routes through it: `chunkIndexForId` (model.ts:137-143), used by render.ts:127, classic-overlays.ts:56, chunk-grid-classic.ts:82, classicEditChunkCells (classicLevelStore.ts:801). The loop-bit strip `cell & 0x7f` is applied consistently at ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:471/490/943 and usage-index.ts:59/144.

The loop-flag stamp path cannot arm bit 7 over air: ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:904 `s.stampLoop && id >= 1 && id <= 0x7f ? id | 0x80 : id`, and the eyedrop at :947 only re-arms it for a real id. (The hole is the MCP path — see A2.)

Ring group expansion is a faithful port: `RING_POS_DATA` (viewport-math.ts:287-294) is byte-for-byte s1disasm/_incObj/25, 37 Rings.asm:23-43, and `ringGroupPositions` (:305-319) reproduces `andi.w #7` + the `cmpi #7 → moveq #6` 8-ring guard (asm:64-74) and `lsr.b #4` orientation nibble (asm:78).

objpos entry format matches the engine and round-trips byte-identically on all 18 profiled files (including the 0xFF tail padding via `originalLength`): 6-byte entries, BE x, yw with bit15=yflip / bit14=xflip / bits0..11=y, id byte bit7=respawn — s1-objpos.ts:34-95, verified against every objpos/*.bin the s1 profile references. (The 12 decode failures I saw are objpos/platforms/*.bin, which are moving-platform path data and are NOT referenced by the profile.)

Collision shape tables are decoded with correct sign handling: `new Int8Array(b.subarray(...))` (s1-collision-shapes.ts:32) performs ToInt8 per element, matching the engine's `ext.w` at FindFloor asm:154; the tables are read-only in the model (`doc.collision.shapes`) and never written back, which is correct since they are global engine data.

Collision inheritance on block cloning is handled deliberately and correctly in both paint paths: `classicPaintSurface` copies `colind[sourceBlockId]` onto the clone (classicLevelStore.ts:925-935), `classicAddBlock` does the same from `opts.sourceBlockId` (:1250-1255), and `planCanvasCommit`'s block interning keys identity on `(tiles, flips, palette, colind)` and refuses to reuse a look-alike block with different collision (classic-commit-plan.ts:364-391), while chunk cells keep the displaced cell's flips and solidity (:409-423).

Block reclaim is conservative and cannot strand a live reference: `computeReclaim` (classic-commit-plan.ts:180-204) reclaims a block only when EVERY chunk referencing it is being replaced, never block 0, never tile 0, and skips reserved/anim/locked tiles.

Zone-art file paths are consistent per zone in the profile (all three GHZ acts → map16/GHZ.eni, map256/GHZ.kos, collide/GHZ.bin, etc.), matching the `zoneart:<zone>` undo document; SBZ act 3 correctly borrows LZ art/collision (profiles/s1.ts:480-497), matching the ROM's LZ-act-4 arrangement.

Undo stacks are dropped on every act load (`disposeStacksFor` for both the outgoing and incoming ref, classicLevelStore.ts:356-357), so a zone-art snapshot taken under SBZ acts 1/2 (SBZ art) can never be replayed onto SBZ act 3 (LZ art).

The save path's source of truth is `WriteResult.files`, never `written` (classic-save.ts:59), self-check errors abort before any byte reaches disk (:57), and `domainsToClear` only clears a domain when every one of its files landed (:145-159) — a partial save leaves the rest dirty for a retry.

The compression codecs are round-trip verified against the real disasm files by the repo's own golden suite plus CI-safe vectors (src/core/formats/classic/__tests__/s1-compression-goldens.test.ts), and the write path re-decodes every compressed buffer with the real decoder before emitting (s1-io.ts:398-417) — that gate is real, unlike the colind one in A7.
All 205 tests in src/core/formats/classic, src/core/level-classic and classic-commit-plan pass at the pinned commit.

findings.title: MCP get_classic_level silently destroys unsaved classic edits + undo history
findings.claim: The agent/MCP `get_classic_level` handler calls `useClassicLevelStore.getState().openAct(ref)` unconditionally, and `openAct` disposes both undo stacks and resets `dirty` to `{}` before re-reading from disk — so any unsaved classic edits are destroyed with no confirmation, no error, and no way back, even when the requested act is the one already open.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/agent/agent-handler.ts:620-625 — `classic-get-level` looks the ref up in `zoneTree` and immediately `await useClassicLevelStore.getState().openAct(ref)`; there is no dirty check and no early-return when `ref` equals the currently-loaded act. src/renderer/state/classicLevelStore.ts:356-357 `disposeStacksFor(get().ref); disposeStacksFor(ref);` (drops `level:<zone>:<act>` AND `zoneart:<zone>` history) and :358-387 `const fresh = { dirty: {} as DirtyDomains, ... }` which is spread into every `set` below, then :401 `const doc = await handle.levels.read(ref)` re-reads from disk. The UI path deliberately does NOT do this: src/renderer/shell/tab-activation/level.ts:3-6 and :56-58 route a dirty classic act to `{kind:'classic-confirm'}` (Save & switch / Discard / Cancel) precisely because "openAct resets doc + dirty + undo history". The same agent file already applies the fail-closed pattern to the sibling tool: agent-handler.ts:575-584 `if (planProjectOpen(currentOpenDirtySnapshot()).kind === 'confirm') throw new Error('Unsaved changes present ...')` for `classic-open-project` — so the omission at :625 is a gap, not a policy. Failure scenario: agent calls `edit_chunk`/`set_colind`/`place_object` on GHZ act 1, then calls `get_classic_level('ghz',1)` to verify its own work; the act is re-read from disk and every uncommitted edit plus the entire undo timeline is gone, and the tool returns a successful-looking payload describing the on-disk state.
findings.fix: In `agent-handler.ts` `case 'classic-get-level'`, (a) return the current doc without re-reading when `ls.ref` already matches `req.zone`/`req.act` and status is 'ready', and (b) for a genuine switch, apply the same fail-closed guard used at :579 — throw when `Object.values(useClassicLevelStore.getState().dirty).some(Boolean)` rather than calling `openAct`. Alternatively give `openAct` an explicit `{ allowDiscard: boolean }` and make the default refuse.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced end-to-end and reproduced empirically; could not refute. (1) agent-handler.ts:621-625 `classic-get-level` calls `useClassicLevelStore.getState().openAct(ref)` unconditionally — no dirty check, no same-ref early return. (2) classicLevelStore.ts:349-357 `openAct` immediately does `disposeStacksFor(get().ref); disposeStacksFor(ref);` (drops both the `level:<zone>:<act>` and `zoneart:<zone>` stacks) with no short-circuit above it; :362 `dirty: {}` is inside the `fresh` object spread into every later `set`; :401 `const doc = await handle.levels.read(ref)` replaces the doc. (3) The real S1 adapter's read (src/core/project/s1/index.ts:365-392) always calls `readS1Level` from disk — the `readStates` map at :356 is write-side bookkeeping ("so write() can re-pair it with the (edited) doc"), not a doc cache, so nothing returns the edited doc. (4) No upstream guard: `registerAgentHandler`/`handleAgentRequest` (agent-handler.ts:46-58) is a bare try/catch dispatcher, and the file's only fail-closed guard is at :575-584 for `classic-open-project`; src/main/editor-methods.ts:115 exposes the tool over MCP ungated. (5) The UI counter-path is even stronger than the seat claimed: `planLevelActivation` (shell/tab-activation/level.ts:56-59) has BOTH a same-act no-op (`return {kind:'none'}`) and a `classic-confirm` for dirty, neither of which the agent path has; the file header at :3-6 states outright that "openAct resets doc + dirty + undo history".

Empirical repro (scratchpad-only test cloned from the repo's own agent-handler.classic harness; repo unmodified): open ghz/1 ready → agent `classic-place-object` (objects 1→2, dirty set, layout stack canUndo=true) → agent `classic-get-level('ghz',1)` on the SAME open act. Output: reads from disk: 1 / objects after: 1 / dirty after: {} / canUndo after: false / tool reported objects: 1. The unsaved edit and the entire undo timeline are destroyed and the tool returns a successful-looking payload describing on-disk state.

Severity: critical is correct per the rubric (silent loss of user work, no confirmation, no recovery via undo), and it is reachable on the most natural agent sequence (edit, then read back to verify) as well as destroying a human's unsaved UI edits mid-session. The only nuance is that the tool description says "Open and read one act" — but the UI's equivalent open is confirm-guarded for exactly this reason and the sibling agent tool is fail-closed, so this is a gap, not a policy.

findings.title: Layout byte $80 (loop flag over air) passes validation and makes the engine read an odd RAM address
findings.claim: `classicSetLayoutCells` validates the MASKED engine id (`chunkId & 0x7f`) against the pool but never rejects the one byte where the loop flag is set over air, $80; the editor draws that cell as air, while S1's FindNearestTile takes the `.specialtile` branch, computes a1 = $FFFFFE01 (odd) and the caller's `move.w (a1),d0` raises a 68000 address error.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/state/classicLevelStore.ts:769-774: `if (!isInt(c.chunkId) || c.chunkId < 0 || c.chunkId > 0xff) return err(...)` then `if ((c.chunkId & 0x7f) > doc.chunks.length) return err(...)`. For c.chunkId = 0x80: 0x80 & 0x7f = 0, and `0 > 82` is false, so the byte is accepted. Engine trace, s1disasm/_incObj/sub FindNearestTile & FindFloor & FindWall.asm: :22 `moveq #$FFFFFFFF,d1`; :24 `move.b (a1,d0.w),d1` → d1=$FFFFFF80; :25 `beq .blanktile` not taken (byte is $80, not 0); :26 `bmi .specialtile` taken; :68 `andi.w #$7F,d1` → d1=$FFFF0000; :77 `subq.b #1,d1` → d1=$FFFF00FF (note this branch has no `ext.w`, unlike the normal path at :29); :78 `ror.w #7,d1` → low word $00FF rotated right 7 = $FE01 → d1=$FFFFFE01; :79-86 add only even offsets ($1E0/$1E masks); :87 `movea.l d1,a1`; back at FindFloor :113 `move.w (a1),d0` on an odd address. Editor side renders it harmlessly: ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:471 `const chunkId = cell & 0x7f` → 0 → air, plus a loop glyph at :478. The UI stamp cannot produce it (ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:904 guards `id >= 1 && id <= 0x7f`), but the MCP `set_layout_region` schema accepts 0..255 per cell (src/main/editor-methods.ts:120-122) and routes straight to `classicSetLayoutCells` (agent-handler.ts:645-655). Every other loop byte $81..$FF is already rejected by the pool check whenever `chunkId & 0x7f > chunks.length`, so $80 is the sole hole.
findings.fix: In `classicSetLayoutCells`, reject a byte with bit 7 set whose masked id is 0: `if ((c.chunkId & 0x80) && (c.chunkId & 0x7f) === 0) return err('$80 is not a valid layout byte — air ($00) cannot carry the loop flag')`. Same rule belongs in the `set_layout_region` zod schema description.

findings.title: Classic collision-angle needle is drawn mirrored (missing sign negation)
findings.claim: `drawCollision` converts the S1 angle byte to a needle with `a = (ang/256)*2π` and then draws it in a y-up (CCW) frame, but S1 angle bytes are clockwise-positive; every non-flat angle tick is therefore mirrored about the horizontal, showing a down-right needle over an up-right slope.
findings.evidence: src/renderer/components/classic/classic-overlays.ts:84-92: `const ang = angles[shapeIndex] ?? 0; const a = (ang / 256) * Math.PI * 2; ... ctx.moveTo(mx - Math.cos(a)*len, my + Math.sin(a)*len); ctx.lineTo(mx + Math.cos(a)*len, my - Math.sin(a)*len);` — the drawn direction vector in screen space (y down) is (cos a, −sin a), i.e. `a` is treated as counter-clockwise. Ground truth measured from the disasm data: shape $50 in collide/Collision Array (Normal).bin is an EXACT 45° ramp rising to the right (heights = [1,2,…,16]) and collide/Angle Map.bin[$50] = $E0. $E0/256*360 = 315°, so the code draws (cos315, −sin315) = (+0.707, +0.707) = right-and-DOWN for a surface that rises right — mirrored. Aurora's own aeon renderer already encodes the correct convention and says so: src/core/collision/collision-shape-draw.ts:124-128 ("The engine angle is clockwise in screen space (y down) … so negate the angle") calls `needleEndpoints(-deg, …)`. classic-overlays.ts has no such negation. Same file also ignores the chunk cell's x/y flips for the angle, while the engine flips it (FindFloor asm :137-147: `not.w d1 / neg.b (a4)` for xflip and `addi.b #$40 / neg.b / subi.b #$40` for yflip) — so a mirrored slope's needle is doubly wrong.
findings.fix: Use `const a = -(ang / 256) * Math.PI * 2;` (or reuse `needleEndpoints` from core/collision/collision-shape-draw.ts so the two renderers cannot drift), and apply the engine's flip math to the angle before drawing: negate for `cell.xf`, and `(-ang - 0x80) & 0xFF` for `cell.yf`.

findings.title: colind shorter than the block list: unreachable via set-colind, rendered as air, and zero-filled on save over what the ROM reads as full-solid
findings.claim: S1 colind files are legitimately shorter than the block list (GHZ ships 410 bytes for 439 blocks; SBZ 600 for 602), and the ROM resolves the overhang from the adjacent zone's table. Aurora models the overhang as shape 0 everywhere: the overlay draws no collision for it, `classicSetColind` refuses to address it at all, and any command that grows the table writes literal 0 bytes over it.
findings.evidence: Measured from the disasm (kosinski/enigma-decoded via the repo's own codecs): GHZ map16 = 439 blocks vs collide/GHZ.bin = 410 bytes; SBZ = 602 blocks vs 600 bytes. sonic.asm:4849-4853 places `Col_GHZ` immediately before `Col_LZ` (GHZ.bin is 410 bytes so the `even` is a no-op), so GHZ block ids 410..438 read LZ.bin[0..28] in the real ROM. Four GHZ chunk cells reference such blocks WITH solidity — chunk fileIdx 45 (engine id 46) cells 144/145 → blocks 417/418, chunk fileIdx 46 (engine id 47) cells 145/146 → blocks 421/422, all solidity 1 — and their ROM colind byte is 255, whose entry in Collision Array (Normal).bin is [16×16] = a FULL SOLID block. Aurora: src/renderer/components/classic/classic-overlays.ts:67 `const shapeIndex = d.collision.colind[cell.block] ?? 0;` → undefined → 0 → :68 `continue` (drawn as air). src/renderer/state/classicLevelStore.ts:1137 `if (!isInt(blockId) || blockId < 0 || blockId >= colind.length) return err(...)` — the only write command for colind cannot address block 410..438 at all, i.e. the exact ids whose collision is currently ROM-implicit. And classicLevelStore.ts:1246-1255 (`classicAddBlock`) / :925-935 (`classicPaintSurface`) / :1050-1057 (`classicCommitCanvas`) all grow the table to `nextBlocks.length` with 0 fill and set `dirty.colind = true`, so the next save emits a 439-byte GHZ.bin in which those four cells become passable. (Chunks $2E/$2F are not placed in stock ghz1/2/3, so the stock game is unaffected today — the hazard fires the moment a user stamps them or authors any solid cell on a block past the table end.)
findings.fix: Read the colind table at least `doc.blocks.length` long — the adapter knows the resolved path and the next zone's file, so either pad from the following blob (faithful) or, at minimum, drop the `blockId >= colind.length` bound in `classicSetColind` (grow instead, like classicAddBlock does) and surface the overhang in the overlay as 'unknown collision (past end of table)' rather than silently as air.

findings.title: Object save re-sorts by X on any edit; the justifying comment names one act when five are affected, and GHZ3's sort swaps two respawn slots
findings.claim: `writeS1Level` stable-sorts the object list by X whenever it differs from disk, justified by a comment claiming only GHZ act 3 is non-ascending. Five of the eighteen profiled acts are non-ascending, and for GHZ act 3 the sort reorders two remember-flagged objects, remapping their respawn-table slots.
findings.evidence: src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:531-534 states "not every real file is strictly X-ascending: GHZ act 3 carries one 64px inversion the loader tolerates", and :536-539 `const emit = objectsEqual(doc.objects, read.objposOriginal) ? read.objposOriginal : [...doc.objects].sort((a, b) => a.x - b.x);`. Decoding every objpos file the profile actually references (src/core/project/profiles/s1.ts:214-491) with the repo's own `decodeS1Objpos` gives inversions in FIVE files, not one: ghz3 (REV01) 1 inversion / 3 entries move, syz1 1 / 2, lz2 2 / 6, slz3 2 / 6, sbz2 1 / 3. S1 assigns respawn slots dynamically by streaming order, not by a stored index — s1disasm/_inc/ObjPosLoad.asm:34 `move.w #$101,(a2)+` (counter starts at 1), :72-77 `bpl .no_respawn / move.b (a2),d2 / addq.b #1,(a2)`, :293 `move.b d2,obRespawnNo(a1)` — so reordering two remember-flagged entries swaps which respawn bit each one owns. Comparing the remember-flagged sequence before/after a stable sort: ghz3 CHANGES at respawn slot 49 (orig index 70, id $22 x=2976 ↔ orig index 71, id $25 x=2912); syz1/lz2/slz3/sbz2 do not change respawn order (only inert entries move). Failure scenario: user nudges one object in GHZ act 3 and saves; three entries are reordered and objects $22 and $25 exchange respawn slots, so a death/restart restores the wrong 'already collected' state for that pair.
findings.fix: Either preserve on-disk order for untouched entries (splice edits in place rather than re-sorting the whole list), or keep the sort but correct the comment and note the respawn-slot consequence; at minimum surface a save-time warning naming the reordered entries. The comment must not claim GHZ act 3 is the only non-ascending file.

findings.title: classicSetColind allows writing colind[0], which the engine can never consult (block 0 short-circuits)
findings.claim: FindFloor tests the block id BEFORE solidity and treats block 0 as blank, so colind[0] is dead data. `classicSetColind` accepts blockId 0, and the overlay would then draw collision on every chunk cell holding block 0 with non-zero solidity — collision the engine never applies.
findings.evidence: Engine order, s1disasm/_incObj/sub FindNearestTile & FindFloor & FindWall.asm:113-118: `move.w (a1),d0 / move.w d0,d4 / andi.w #$7FF,d0 / beq.s .isblank` (block id 0 short-circuits) and only THEN `btst d5,d4 / bne .issolid`, with the colind lookup at :129-132. Aurora's overlay inverts that order and omits the block-0 rule: src/renderer/components/classic/classic-overlays.ts:66 `if (!cell || cell.solidity === 0) continue;` then :67 `const shapeIndex = d.collision.colind[cell.block] ?? 0;` — no `cell.block === 0` check. src/renderer/state/classicLevelStore.ts:1136-1142 validates only `blockId >= 0` and `blockId < colind.length`, so `classicSetColind([{blockId:0,value:7}])` is accepted (and is exactly what src/renderer/state/__tests__/classicLevelStore.test.ts:328 asserts succeeds). The codebase states the rule correctly elsewhere and enforces it there — src/core/art/classic-commit-plan.ts:17-22 ("S1's FindFloor short-circuits on block number 0 BEFORE it tests solidity, so block 0 can never carry collision") and classicLevelStore.ts:1043 `if (blockId < 1) return err('block 0 is engine-blank and cannot be written')` — so this is a per-command inconsistency. Harmless on stock data (measured: colind[0] === 0 in all six zones, and no chunk cell in any zone pairs block 0 with non-zero solidity), but an agent write makes the overlay lie.
findings.fix: Reject blockId 0 in `classicSetColind` with the same message classicCommitCanvas uses, and add the `cell.block === 0 → continue` short-circuit to `drawCollision` so the overlay's evaluation order matches FindFloor even if the table is edited externally.

findings.title: The colind save self-check is a tautology — it cannot fail
findings.claim: `writeS1Level`'s colind gate re-decodes the buffer it just encoded and compares it to the same source array, but both codecs are `slice()`, so the comparison is `bytesEqual(x.slice().slice(), x)` — always true. The module docblock advertises this domain as gated by a real decoder round-trip.
findings.evidence: src/core/level-classic/s1-io.ts:561-569 `emitVerified(read.paths.colind, encodeS1ColInd(doc.collision.colind), decodeS1ColInd, (b) => bytesEqual(b, doc.collision.colind), 'colind')`, with src/core/formats/classic/s1-colind.ts:9-15 `decodeS1ColInd = b.slice()` and `encodeS1ColInd = c.slice()`. There is no input that can make this branch push to `errors`. The docblock at s1-io.ts:57-62 claims "Compressed and directly-encoded domains are re-decoded with the REAL decoder and deep-compared to the doc structure they came from (`emitCompressed` / `emitVerified`)" and singles out the palette as "the one exception"; colind is a second exception. (Contrast the objpos gate at :540-546, which is real: an object at x=$FFFF would re-decode as the terminator and fail.) No data loss today because the codec is identity, but the gate provides no protection if colind ever gains a real encoder, and it inflates the apparent coverage of the save path.
findings.fix: Either state in the docblock that colind (like palette) has no codec and its gate only proves length/identity, or replace it with a check that actually constrains something (e.g. every value in 0..255 and length >= doc.blocks.length).
